Vanessa: Blimey! My computer is not working! I bought it last month!
Peter: It's probably nothing serious. Maybe I'll be able to fix it for you.
Vanessa: How much do you know about computer repair?
Peter: I had to fix mine recently. I kept getting the blue screen of death.
Vanessa: Oh, I hate when that happens.

Peter: Can I see what kind of error message you are getting?
Vanessa: I don't even have a message! The screen keeps blinking and then turns black. All I hear is this annoying bleep!
Peter: When do you remember having this problem for the first time?
Vanessa: I'm not sure. I blame that tech guy! I'm so disappointed right now!

Peter: I think technology makes you irritable. Here, take my computer for now.
Vanessa: Are you sure you don't you need it for work?
Peter: I'll use my desktop at the office. This is my personal laptop. You're welcome to borrow it if you want.
Vanessa: Thanks, Peter. You're such a nice bloke!
Peter: Aw, you're going to make me blush now! That's what friends are for.

Stressing New Information in Questions With Sentences
When you want to stress new information, you use different intonation and stress on the “new”  idea. You can stress questions with sentences in the same way.
You usually stress content words in a sentence. Content words are the words that carry the most meaning (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, etc.).

When you want to introduce new information in a conversation, you can choose to put the stress and the intonation on the “new” idea. This helps the listener understand that you want to stress that word and that it is important.

Example:
Sally: I'm having problems with my computer.
Peter: What kind of problems?
Sentence stress gives English its rhythm or beat.
Word stress is emphasis on one syllable within a word.
Sentence stress is emphasis on certain words within a sentence.
Most sentences have two basic types of words:

content words
  • Content words are the important or key words in a sentence. They provide the meaning of the sentence.

structure words
  • Structure words are not important words. They are small words that you use to make the sentence correct.
When you stress these “new” words, your voice will rise slightly (intonation).
